title: test(service-datasource): the pool-support and driver-factory suites run under 10 s (two #23184 rows)
body:
Refs #23184 (service-datasource rows: datasource-pool-support, default-datasource-driver-factory)
Clause-②: no

## Rows answered

Both rows of the card's `@objectstack/service-datasource` list:

- `src/__tests__/datasource-pool-support.test.ts`, listed at 17.6 s (run `38294929860`);
- `src/__tests__/default-datasource-driver-factory.test.ts`, listed at 10.6 s (run `38217670691`).

The pin is the next refresh PR's list: it should name neither file. The card stays open for its other rows: the three remaining `plugin-auth` rows (org-create-posture-gate, implicit-account-linking, dev-admin-seed-credential-gate) and the `plugin-security` and `organizations` rows.

The diff is tests only: 5 module-top side-effect import lines and their comments in the two test files, +44 / -0. No production file, option, constant, timeout or export changes. Every `it(`, `describe(` and `expect(` line in both files is byte-identical to the base and in the same order.

## Where the time went

A probe at the base (temporary, deleted; two runs per file, each in a fresh vitest worker) timed every load the files' cases trigger, in the order they trigger them:

| load, in case order | pool-support order | driver-factory order |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `@objectstack/core`, first load | 8.9 / 7.7 s | 7.1 / 9.5 s |
| `@objectstack/driver-sql` (knex) | 1.32 / 0.54 s | 0.57 / 0.80 s |
| `@objectstack/driver-memory`, after core | 0.46 / 0.25 s | 0.26 / 0.32 s |
| `@objectstack/driver-mongodb`, after core | 0.17 / 0.16 s | 0.14 / 0.24 s |
| `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm`, after driver-sql | n/a | 0.04 / 0.04 s |
| the behaviour itself: each `create()`, the wasm connect, sync and round trip | 2 to 18 ms each | about 0.1 s first, 10 ms after |

So nearly all of each file's clocked wall was one module load. The factory reaches every driver through a lazy `await import()`, and every driver imports `@objectstack/core`. This package's `vitest.config.ts` aliases `@objectstack/core` to `packages/core/src/index.ts`, so the first case to build a real driver paid a cold vite transform of core's whole source graph inside its clocked window. In `datasource-pool-support` that was `memory WITHOUT a pool still builds exactly as before` (8.1 s of the file's 9.3 s). In `default-datasource-driver-factory` it was `builds a file-backed SqliteWasmDriver that connects and round-trips` (11.4 s of 12.4 s). No case waits on a timer, a retry back-off, an idle or acquire timeout, or a live database. Every postgres, mysql and mongodb case builds a driver without connecting.

## What changed

Each file now pays that load at module top, in collection, following the AGENTS.md convention that clocked windows measure behaviour, never loading (the clocked-window rule of `check-test-source-alias`). The factory's own lazy imports stay where they are; the module cache hands them the instances already loaded.

- `datasource-pool-support.test.ts`: `import '@objectstack/core'` and `import '@objectstack/driver-sql'`.
- `default-datasource-driver-factory.test.ts`: the same two, plus `import '@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm'`.

Three drivers are left out on purpose, and each still loads inside its first case:

- `@objectstack/driver-memory` (0.2 to 0.5 s once core is loaded): every module binding of it is a ruled census entry. A first cut that imported it here turned `check:driver-memory-census` red, because a new binding needs a maintainer ruling.
- `@objectstack/driver-mongodb` (0.1 to 0.3 s): this package's tests reach it only through the factory, so a test-file import is a new unaliased artifact import. The same first cut turned `check:test-source-alias` red. Aliasing it would change a config file outside this card's surface.
- `@objectstack/driver-turso`: the turso missing-package case stages its absence without `vi.resetModules()`, so the factory's own lazy import must be that package's first. The `sqlite-wasm` absence case resets the module registry before it mocks, so loading that package at module top is the same condition the construction suites already created for it.

## Measurements

Each figure is vitest's per-file duration (JSON reporter `endTime - startTime`, the module-line duration the refresh reads): `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 FILE --reporter=verbose --reporter=json`, in `packages/services/service-datasource`, under `os-verify-lock`, on a shared 4-vCPU box. The final before and after runs were interleaved at the final head, with the before leg being the base file copied to a temporary name (deleted afterwards), so both legs saw the same load.

| file | before, base `f1e21c4f45` alone (load 1.3 to 1.6) | before, interleaved at `a573f9c57a` (load 1.6 to 3.0) | after, interleaved at `a573f9c57a` | median after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| datasource-pool-support | 9312 / 8973 / 9337 ms | 8967 / 8577 / 8287 ms | 611 / 572 / 704 ms | **0.61 s** |
| default-datasource-driver-factory | 12412 / 9129 / 9501 ms | 9082 / 10044 / 9393 ms | 751 / 711 / 750 ms | **0.75 s** |

**The load is moved, not removed.** vitest's whole-file `Duration` (collection plus run) is unchanged within noise: pool-support 12.70 / 11.50 / 11.73 s before against 12.05 / 12.18 / 12.38 s after, and driver-factory 12.48 / 13.40 / 13.06 s before against 13.19 / 12.48 / 13.44 s after. The `import` phase grew from about 3 s to about 11 to 12.5 s per file. What the change buys is that no test or hook clock contains a compiler run any more. It does not make the package's test job faster.

**CI projection.** The per-file CI captures of recent hourly runs are NOT MEASURED. The `test-core-timing-table` artifact of hourly run `38773780951` redirects to `productionresultssa5.blob.core.windows.net`, which this container's egress proxy refuses (CONNECT 403). The ratios therefore come from the card's own readings against the interleaved before medians: pool-support 17.6 s against 8.58 s is a ratio of 2.05, which projects to **1.25 s**; driver-factory 10.6 s against 9.39 s is 1.13, which projects to **0.85 s**. At a 4.0 ratio, the worst post-landing ratio an earlier slice of this card read, they project to 2.4 s and 3.0 s.

## Proof that every case still runs and still asserts the same

- **Case lists:** 72 of 72 and 50 of 50 passed in every run, before and after.
- **Static lines:** the `it(` / `it.each(` / `describe(` / `expect(` lines are byte-identical to the base and in order: 72 / 0 / 8 / 177 for pool-support, and 45 / 1 / 10 / 105 for driver-factory.
- **Runtime assertions:** a temporary copy of each file recorded `expect.getState().assertionCalls` per case, at the base and at the head. The per-case counts are identical: 210 assertions over 72 cases, and 128 over 50 cases. No case asserts nothing.
- **Same module instances (temporary probe, deleted):** with `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` imported at module top, the factory's `sqlite`, `postgres`, `mysql` and `sqlite-wasm` drivers are each `instanceof` the class the test file imported (4 of 4). The first memory `create()` then took 241 ms, against 8 s with core not yet loaded.
- **No mutation is owed.** The change moves where a module load is paid. It changes no tested behaviour, and no case asserts timing, so reverting it reddens nothing. The interleaved before leg is that revert, measured.

## Tests and gates (final head `a573f9c57a`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-datasource run typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc --listFilesOnly` lists both changed files in the package's program.
- The whole `@objectstack/service-datasource` suite with `--maxWorkers=2`: 45 of 45 files, 838 of 838 tests passed.
- ESLint on the 2 changed files with `--no-inline-config`: exit 0. The control-byte scan of both files found 0 hits.
- `skip-changeset`: the package ships `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. The comment marker of this change has 0 hits in its built `dist`, and the positive control `createDefaultDatasourceDriverFactory` has 4.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 52 commands, the same 52 as the seat's lead. All 52 exit 0 at `a573f9c57a`, each run separately with the exit code captured before any pipe, and `--ran` reports 52 derived, 52 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED and 0 UNRUN. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` ran after a full `turbo run build` (75 of 75 tasks). A first sweep at the first cut (`ab97ec143f`) had `check:driver-memory-census` and `check:test-source-alias` red, which is what narrowed the import list (above); every other family was green there too.
- `check:engine-double-contract` printed its repo-wide census line verbatim: `UNRECOGNISED [engine-double-contract]: 22 construct(s) in packages, examples declare a scanned verb (delete, update, findOne) alongside engine siblings, and this gate could not read the implementation -- so they are in NEITHER the pinned population nor the ledger.` Its output names neither changed file, and this diff adds no construct.
- The full lint farm, Test Core, the dogfood jobs and the type-check lanes belong to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **The core transform recurs per file.** About 7 to 9.5 s of cold transform of `@objectstack/core`'s source is paid by every test file in this package whose cases load a driver, once per worker, because the package's vitest config aliases `@objectstack/core` to source. The alias is the intended repair of `check:test-source-alias`, and that gate's header names aliased dependencies as outside its clocked-window population ("widening the population is a different card"), which is also why the gate was green over these two files at `69351e985a` (measured, exit 0). This is an observation, not a defect, and no carrier is named.
- **A stale reading in `vitest.config.ts`.** The config's `testTimeout` comment cites `sqlite WITHOUT a pool` as about 1.1 s idle, paying the driver-sql import. After this change that case runs in 28 to 43 ms. The 60 s timeout itself is untouched (no timeout was raised or lowered), and the comment is outside this card's surface. Noted, not filed.
- The per-file CI captures cannot be read from a cloud container (blob-storage egress is refused), as the previous slice also recorded. This is an environment fact, not a repo defect.
